title: Melatonin-conjugated polycaprolactone nanoparticles enable targeted temozolomide delivery with improved pharmacokinetics, colon accumulation and safety in colorectal cancer
content: Temozolomide (TMZ) has therapeutic limitations in colorectal cancer (CRC) due to poor solubility and systemic toxicity. We proposed the development of biodegradable polycaprolactone (PCL) nanoparticles attached to melatonin (MLT) for targeted site-specific delivery of TMZ in colorectal cancer. Network pharmacology and molecular modeling studies demonstrated strong interactions (docking scores as low as −6.28) with cancer targets (MAPK8, MTOR) that modulate MAPK and PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathways in CRC. The nanoparticles (TMZ–PCL–MLT-NPs) were optimized to yield a final particle size of 199.8 ± 7.1 nm, zeta potential of −29.9 ± 1.2 mV, and a drug encapsulated efficiency of 68.4 ± 1.9%. In vitro studies demonstrated that TMZ–PCL–MLT-NPs was better than free TMZ, with cell viability detected to be 35–45% lower. Based on pharmacokinetics studies, we observed 7.45 ± 0.89 hours half-life (free TMZ 1.88 ± 0.23 h, p = 0.009) and the AUC was 2.8 times increased (434.2 ± 22.3 vs. 156.4 ± 15.6 µg h ml−1). Biodistribution showed an increase in colon accumulation (8.23 ± 1.30 µg g−1vs. 6.01 ± 1.10 µg g−1, p = 0.02). Histopathology reports showed no toxicity to organs measured, and was therefore considered biocompatible. Our formulation also had antimicrobial activity against E. coli, which would also limit potential infection risk during treatment. This novel and comprehensive approach allows the TMZ–PCL–MLT-NPs system to emerge as an attractive consideration for clinical translation in patients with CRC, and the potential for better clinical effects, with an improved safety profile.
